description:
EXECUTE a unified screen = universe ∩ fundamental ∩ technical ∩ options (any leg optional; each grammar resolved
    server-side — key or plain English). Returns {universe, count, sort, executed_criteria (the resolved request that ran — save/re-run it verbatim), results:[{head_listing_id, ticker, name, score,
    matched_legs, matched:{ta, fundamental:{<metric>:{value, basis, window?, series?, periods?}}}, context}], notes}.
    Evidence keys == the leg name you sent (TA→matched.ta, fundamentals→matched.fundamental, NOT technical/financial);
    `matched_legs` lists which leg(s) a row passed. A thin intersection adds partial:true + per-leg near-misses — never
    present a partial/one-leg row as a full match; read `notes` (names the tighter leg + how to broaden).
    Time windows are PER-LEG: TA 'within last N bars' = top-level `window_bars`; a fundamental trend's span = that
    condition's `N`. Options leg is US-optionable only (~557 → US-capped); sort='options' ranks by it; an
    options-vs-price divergence = just send the phrase in `options`. FAILS LOUD: an unsupported pattern/operand/concept
    returns a 400, so count:0 with NO error = a VALID query that matched zero now (loosen / widen window_bars, don't say
    'can't do X'); `notes` may say 'insufficient history' (not a no-match) or which basis was screened. Over-fetches a
    ~4× buffer (cap 100) so 'show me more' is served from these rows — don't re-call.

ScreenCondition.description:
ONE AND-ed condition. COMMON form = `concept` (the METRIC) + `pattern` (the SHAPE) + its value. RELATION form
(rare) = compare two metrics: metricA + relation + metricB. SHARED RULES for every text field below: send an exact
key OR plain English — the server resolves it (no separate resolver step); ENGLISH only; a metric's change-over-time
is a `pattern`, never part of `concept`. NUMBER SCALE: ratios/margins/yields/growth-rates are FRACTIONS (0.20 = 20%);
P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA and coverage multiples are RAW (15 = a P/E of 15).

N.description: Window = number of `basis` periods for growth/consecutive patterns (default years; quarters if basis='quarterly'). Supply only when the user stated the span; else the pattern's default.
N.title: N

band.description: RELATION ratio_near: half-width tolerance as a fraction of target (default 0.10 = ±10%).
band.title: Band

basis.description: Period type — default annual; set 'quarterly' (QoQ / 'N quarters in a row') or 'ttm' only when the user named it. Separate from `pattern`; if unsupported the server screens what it can and notes it.
basis.title: Basis

cagr.description: compound_growth/decline only: ANNUALIZED rate per year as a fraction ('15%/yr over 5y' → N:5, cagr:0.15). NOT the whole-window total (that's total_change).
cagr.title: Cagr

concept.description: The METRIC (statement line / ratio / valuation multiple): pe, roe, net_margin, revenue, 'gross margin'.
concept.title: Concept

measure.description: Quarterly consecutive_growth only: 'sequential' (default, QoQ) or 'yoy' (each quarter vs the same quarter a year earlier).
measure.title: Measure

metricA.description: RELATION form: first metric. Its GROWTH RATE instead of level → metricA_stat='growth'.
metricA.title: Metrica

metricA_stat.description: RELATION: read metricA as 'level' (default) or 'growth' (its N-year growth %, N default 3).
metricA_stat.title: Metrica Stat

metricB.description: RELATION form: second metric. Its GROWTH RATE → metricB_stat='growth'.
metricB.title: Metricb

multiple.description: RELATION higher/lower_than bound k in 'A vs k×B' (default 1): a FRACTION for 'A is k% OF B' (0.15), a direct ratio otherwise (2 = 2×). Ignored by growth_faster/slower_than.
multiple.title: Multiple

params.description: Fallback only — prefer the top-level fields; a nested value here is still read.
params.title: Params

pattern.description: The SHAPE — a LEVEL (above, below, between, low, high, above_average, below_average) or a CHANGE (latest_yoy, consecutive_growth/decline, compound_growth, accelerating). NL ok ('grew every year','above the sector average').
pattern.title: Pattern

percentile.description: Tail fraction for `low`/`high` ('cheapest 10%' → 0.1); default 0.2. Supply only when the user named a tail size.
percentile.title: Percentile

relation.description: RELATION form — metricA vs metricB: higher_than/lower_than (A vs multiple×B), ratio_between (min≤A/B≤max), ratio_near (A/B≈target ±band), growth_faster_than/growth_slower_than (CAGRs). Param: higher/lower→multiple; ratio_between→min+max; ratio_near→target(+band); growth→none. e.g. 'R&D ≥15% of revenue' → metricA=rnd, higher_than, metricB=revenue, multiple=0.15.
relation.title: Relation

target.description: RELATION ratio_near: the A/B ratio to sit near, a FRACTION (0.08 = ~8% of B).
target.title: Target

threshold.description: The number `above`/`below` (REQUIRED for them — no default) or a growth pattern compares against. If the user gave only a vague quality ('cheap','high ROE') with NO number, use a cohort pattern (above_average/below_average/low/high…) which needs none.
threshold.title: Threshold

total_change.description: compound_growth/decline only: CUMULATIVE change over the N-period window as a fraction (1.0 = doubled/halved, 0.5 = +50%/−50%). 'doubled in 2y' → N:2, total_change:1.0. NOT per-year (that's cagr).
total_change.title: Total Change

vs_cohort.description: RARE — usually OMIT: a cohort pattern already compares each stock with ITS OWN GICS sector in its country. Set only for another peer group: {gics?:code-prefix, country?:ISO-2, size?:[tiers], stat?:'pooled'|'median'}, a finer own grain {own:'gics_group'|'gics_industry'}, or {} = the universe's average.
vs_cohort.title: Vs Cohort

ScreenCondition.title: ScreenCondition

TaQual.description: An AND qualifier at a moment — a group of signals combined with OR (≥1 must hold).

any.description: Signals combined with OR; at least one must hold. Max 3.
any.title: Any

within.description: ± tolerance in trading bars around the anchor (default 5; use 0 for a persistent state like 'is above').
within.title: Within

TaQual.title: TaQual

TaSignal.description:
ONE technical signal = a SHAPE (`pattern`) + its operand LINES (`a`/`b`). Each is a key/token OR plain
English — the SERVER resolves each.

a.description: Operand A (SUBJECT line) — a token (close/ema50/rsi/macd_line/adx/stoch_k/bb_upper/senkou_a/tenkan…) or plain English, server-resolved. Cross/touch: the ACTIVE line (two MAs → the faster; price-vs-MA → 'close'). above/below read literally 'a is above/below b' ('price above the 200-day' → a='close',b='ema200'). Non-standard periods (ema45,rsi7) snap to the nearest. Omit for operand-free patterns.
a.title: A

b.description: Operand B — the PASSIVE reference line (token/English) or a numeric level as a string (oscillator-vs-level → '30'/'70'; MACD-vs-signal → 'macd_signal'; two MAs → the slower). For a net-return pattern (net_change_up/down), b = the move magnitude as a FRACTION ('0.30' = 30%). Fibonacci level → fib_618 ('61.8%', 'golden ratio'), fib_382, fib_1000 (100%), fib_1618 … Omit if the pattern has no reference.
b.title: B

for_bars.description: A state/level must have HELD ≥ this many consecutive bars ('above the 200-day for a month' ≈ 20 daily bars); for rising/falling it's a run-length. NOT valid on net_change/crossover/divergence — for 'within the last N bars' use window_bars.
for_bars.title: For Bars

pattern.description: The chart SHAPE — a pattern key or plain English ('golden cross','breaking out of a squeeze'), server-resolved. Keys: above, at_new_high, at_new_low, bb_squeeze, below, converge, crossover_down, crossover_up, divergence_bear, divergence_bull, expand, falling, fib_break_down, fib_break_up, fib_zone, hidden_divergence_bear, hidden_divergence_bull, in_range, kumo_expand, kumo_squeeze, near_high, near_low, near_ma, net_change_down, net_change_up, off_high_by, off_low_by, overbought, oversold, rising, rising_volume, squeeze, squeeze_fired, squeeze_fired_dn, squeeze_fired_up, squeeze_started, touch_down, touch_up, ttm_squeeze, volume_dryup, volume_spike. bb_squeeze = coiling now; squeeze_fired_up/dn = coiled-then-broke, SELF-CONTAINED — use as the anchor, don't chain squeeze-THEN-fire. NO OPERAND NEEDED (omit a/b; a few take an optional b): at_new_high, at_new_low, bb_squeeze, kumo_expand, kumo_squeeze, near_high, near_low, near_ma, rising_volume, squeeze_fired, squeeze_fired_dn, squeeze_fired_up, squeeze_started, ttm_squeeze, volume_dryup, volume_spike. Divergence takes only `a` = the oscillator: rsi (default) or macd; hidden divergence rsi only — other lines are refused. Oscillator band ('RSI 40-50') = ONE in_range (a='rsi', b='40-50'). FIBONACCI (levels of the latest confirmed swing): fib_zone = price testing / sitting at a level NOW; fib_break_up / fib_break_down = the close crossed up / down through a level within window_bars (use these, NOT crossover_*); 'holding above the 61.8%' = above (a='close', b='fib_618'). b = the level: fib_382/500/618 (golden ratio)/786/1000 (100% = the prior swing extreme)/1272/1618/2618/4236; optional swing size fib_minor_618 / fib_major_618 (default mid).
pattern.title: Pattern

timeframe.description: PER-CONDITION chart (1=daily,2=weekly,3=monthly; or the words daily/weekly/monthly) to MIX timeframes — put it on a QUALIFIER (checked on its own chart) while the anchor stays on the screen-level timeframe. e.g. weekly-hold + daily-cross → screen tf=1, qualifier {above,a='close',b='ema50',timeframe:2}. Operand periods are bars of THIS tf. An ANCHOR's tf must equal the screen-level tf (else 400) — put cross-tf tests in a qualifier.
timeframe.title: Timeframe

window_bars.description: PER-SIGNAL lookback in bars — 'holds WITHIN the last N bars' (recency); for a net-return pattern it's the PERIOD the return is measured over ('dropped 30% over 100 days' → window_bars=100). Gives conditions DIFFERENT windows in one screen. Omit → the screen-level default. (Distinct from for_bars = how long a state has held.)
window_bars.title: Window Bars

TaSignal.title: TaSignal

TaStep.description: ONE moment. Multiple steps = a THEN chain (step 0 happens, THEN step 1 …). Same-moment conditions go in ONE step.

anchor.description: Primary signal(s) for this moment; multiple = OR; also the sort key. Max 3.
anchor.title: Anchor

quals.description: Extra conditions that must ALL hold at this moment (AND). Max 4.
quals.title: Quals

TaStep.title: TaStep

asset_type.description: OPTIONAL asset type(s), OR'd: 'Common Stock','ETF','Crypto','Currency','Commodity','Bond','Index','Fund','ADR','REIT'. Crypto≠Currency (forex); gold/silver=Commodity. Omit = all (a company screen usually wants 'Common Stock').
asset_type.title: Asset Type

count_total.description: Set true ONLY when the user asks HOW MANY match ('how many stocks…', 'is it more than 500?'): returns the exact `total` up to 500, else `total_over: 500`. Slower (runs every leg in full) — omit for a normal screen.
count_total.title: Count Total

country.description: OPTIONAL operating-country scope — one or MORE ISO-2 codes, OR'd (a stock matches if in ANY of them). e.g. ['US'] · ['CN','US'] for China+US · ['TH','SG','MY']. Omit = all countries.
country.title: Country

criteria.description: A WHOLE formula in the saved shape — the `executed_criteria` a screen_unified call returned, or the user's saved formula ({universe:{include:[{country,gics,size,theme,asset_type,mcap_min,mcap_max}], exclude:[…]}, ta, fundamental:[{concept,pattern,params}], options:{pattern,horizon}, timeframe, window_bars, dividend}). To change a formula you got back, send it here WITH YOUR CHANGE APPLIED — resolved keys stay as they are, plain-English fields inside are resolved as usual. Works with every `mode`. Do not also send the separate formula fields (fundamental, ta, options, gics, country, …) — one or the other; sort / limit / count_total / mode may go with it.
criteria.title: Criteria

dividend_min_cagr.description: OPTIONAL dividend gate — 5-year dividend CAGR ≥ this % (5 = ≥5%/yr). Needs a fundamental/ta/options base leg too.
dividend_min_cagr.title: Dividend Min Cagr

dividend_min_streak_years.description: OPTIONAL dividend gate — keep stocks with a no-cut dividend streak ≥ N years (reliability streak in a 10-year window, capped at 10; NOT the full age). A membership gate — combine with a fundamental/ta/options base leg (pure dividend screen → screen_dividends).
dividend_min_streak_years.title: Dividend Min Streak Years

exclude_country.description: OPTIONAL — EXCLUDE operating-country(ies), ISO-2. 'global ex-US' = exclude_country=['US']. Universe-level, applies to every leg.
exclude_country.title: Exclude Country

exclude_gics.description: OPTIONAL — EXCLUDE industry/theme CONCEPT(s), CSV, codes or plain English ('banks','AI'); server-resolved & routed same as `gics`. Applies to EVERY leg ('high-yield but NOT banks' = fundamental dividend_yield + exclude_gics='banks'). `gics` INCLUDES; this EXCLUDES.
exclude_gics.title: Exclude Gics

exclude_theme.description: ADVANCED raw-passthrough — EXCLUDE megatrend THEME node_id(s). Normally just name the theme to exclude in `exclude_gics` ('not AI'); the server routes it. Universe-level negation across every leg.
exclude_theme.title: Exclude Theme

fundamental.description: The FUNDAMENTAL leg — AND-ed conditions (each = a METRIC `concept` + a SHAPE `pattern` + its value; key or plain English, server-resolved). e.g. roe>20% & 3y revenue growth → [{concept:'roe',pattern:'above',threshold:0.20},{concept:'revenue',pattern:'consecutive_growth',N:3}]. 🔴 A fundamental trend's TIME SPAN goes in that condition's `N` (periods of its `basis`, annual by default; set basis only for quarterly/TTM) — SEPARATE from the TA leg's window_bars. Omit for a TA-only screen.
fundamental.title: Fundamental

gics.description: OPTIONAL universe SCOPE — industry/theme concept(s), CSV of ATOMIC concepts (decompose 'banks and insurance' → 'banks,insurance'). Each = English ('banks','semiconductors','AI') or a GICS code prefix ('45'=IT sector, '352010'=biotech industry; shorter=broader); the server picks the axis (industry→GICS, megatrend→THEME). Omit = all sectors.
gics.title: Gics

limit.description: How many stocks to SHOW (default 10). Over-fetches a ~4× buffer (capped 100) so 'show me a few more' is served from THIS result — don't re-screen; re-screen only to exceed the buffer.
limit.title: Limit

max_market_cap_usd.description: OPTIONAL ABSOLUTE max market cap USD (2000000000 = under $2bn). Pair with min for a band.
max_market_cap_usd.title: Max Market Cap Usd

min_market_cap_usd.description: OPTIONAL ABSOLUTE min market cap USD (50000000000 = $50bn). Use this (not `size`) for a USD floor / 'under $X' band.
min_market_cap_usd.title: Min Market Cap Usd

mode.description: What to do with the formula. 'run' (default) = screen and return the stocks. 'check' = NO scan, no market data: resolve every field exactly as a run does and validate the formula (rules only, fast) → {ok, executed_criteria, snaps/notes}, or the same needs_rewrite answer (code, path, error, _guide, nearest) when it cannot run — use it to try a formula or a choice BEFORE you offer it. 'count' = 'check' + how many stocks match (exact up to 500, `capped` above) — use it when only how many is needed. No rows in check/count; count_total is for 'run' only.
mode.title: Mode

options.description: The OPTIONS leg — an options-behaviour term, key or plain English ('fear_building','iv_cheap','the crowd getting brave'), server-resolved. Intersects the ~557 US-optionable names showing it; an options-vs-price DIVERGENCE also goes here (the server expands it). US-optionable only. Omit for a non-options screen.
options.title: Options

options_horizon.description: Options horizon: 'long' (default, positioning/conviction) or 'short' (gamma/near-term). Only meaningful with `options`.
options_horizon.title: Options Horizon

size.description: OPTIONAL market-cap size tier(s), OR'd — 'large'|'mid'|'small'|'micro'. RELATIVE per-market MSCI tiers ('small' = small FOR ITS market, not in USD; no separate 'mega'). For an ABSOLUTE USD size / 'under $X' use min/max_market_cap_usd instead. Omit = all sizes.
size.title: Size

sort.description: Rank key: 'ta' (default, TA chain score) · 'options' (use when `options` present) · 'mcap' · a TA-context oscillator ('rsi'/'adx' — 'most overbought'→'rsi') · or any fundamental metric key in the results (pe/roe/…).
sort.title: Sort

ta.description: The TECHNICAL leg — a THEN chain of steps (usually ONE). Each signal = `pattern` (SHAPE) + operands `a`/`b` (LINES), key or plain English, server-resolved. e.g. golden cross + volume spike → [{anchor:[{pattern:'crossover_up',a:'ema50',b:'ema200'}],quals:[{any:[{pattern:'volume_spike'}]}]}]. 'within the last N bars' = each signal's own `window_bars` (else the screen-level default); mix timeframes by setting a qualifier's own `timeframe` (1/2/3). Omit for a fundamentals-only screen.
ta.title: Ta

theme.description: ADVANCED raw-passthrough — megatrend THEME node_id(s), OR'd (core member of ANY). Normally OMIT: name the theme in `gics` ('AI') and the server routes it. Use only with a known node_id.
theme.title: Theme

timeframe.description: Chart for the TA leg: 1=daily (default) · 2=weekly · 3=monthly. TA operand periods & for_bars are counted in BARS of this timeframe.
timeframe.title: Timeframe

window_bars.description: TA-leg LOOKBACK in bars of `timeframe` — how far back a signal may have fired / the span a THEN-chain completes within ('…within the last N days'; 'divergence within 50 days' → 50). Whole `ta` leg; omit → default 30 × number of ta steps. SEPARATE from a fundamental trend's `N`.
window_bars.title: Window Bars

name: screen_unified
title: Unified Screener (Universe × Fundamental × Technical)
